segments.text: Nine friends in a café.
segments.caption: Nine friends in a café.

segments.text: Their average salary? Forty thousand a month.
segments.caption: Their average salary? 40,000 a month.

segments.text: Then a billionaire walks in.
segments.caption: Then a billionaire walks in.

segments.text: Now the average is one crore!
segments.caption: Now the average is 1 crore!

segments.text: One extreme value changed everything.
segments.caption: One extreme value changed everything.

segments.text: That's an outlier!
segments.caption: That's an outlier!

segments.text: An outlier is a value that sits far away from the rest of the data.
segments.caption: An outlier is a value that sits far away from the rest of the data.

segments.text: They come in two kinds.
segments.caption: They come in two kinds.

segments.text: Some are mistakes, like a typo that turns an age of twenty-five into two hundred and fifty.
segments.caption: Some are mistakes, like a typo that turns an age of 25 into 250.

segments.text: Others are real, just rare: a billionaire, a festival sales spike, a fraudulent payment.
segments.caption: Others are real, just rare: a billionaire, a festival sales spike, a fraudulent payment.

segments.text: Either way, they can wreck your analysis.
segments.caption: Either way, they can wreck your analysis.

segments.text: How do you spot one? Use the IQR fence rule.
segments.caption: How do you spot one? Use the IQR fence rule.

segments.text: Here are eleven test scores.
segments.caption: Here are 11 test scores.

segments.text: The middle half: fifty to sixty-two. So the IQR is twelve.
segments.caption: The middle half: 50 to 62. So the IQR is 12.

segments.text: Step one and a half IQRs, that's eighteen, beyond each end.
segments.caption: Step 1.5 IQRs, that's 18, beyond each end.

segments.text: The fences land at thirty-two and eighty.
segments.caption: The fences land at 32 and 80.

segments.text: Ninety-five jumps the fence. Outlier!
segments.caption: 95 jumps the fence. Outlier!

segments.text: First, outliers distort your summary numbers.
segments.caption: First, outliers distort your summary numbers.

segments.text: The mean jumped: forty thousand to one crore!
segments.caption: The mean jumped: 40,000 to 1 crore!

segments.text: The median? Just forty-one thousand.
segments.caption: The median? Just 41,000.

segments.text: And the range? Almost ten crore!
segments.caption: And the range? Almost 10 crore!

segments.text: Second, they can bend a trend.
segments.caption: Second, they can bend a trend.

segments.text: More hours studied, higher scores. A clear rising line.
segments.caption: More hours studied, higher scores. A clear rising line.

segments.text: Now add one student who studied eight hours but missed the exam.
segments.caption: Now add one student who studied 8 hours but missed the exam.

segments.text: The line goes almost flat, as if studying barely helps!
segments.caption: The line goes almost flat, as if studying barely helps!

segments.text: Here's the complete picture.
segments.caption: Here's the complete picture.

segments.text: Outliers drag the average.
segments.caption: Outliers drag the average.

segments.text: They inflate the spread.
segments.caption: They inflate the spread.

segments.text: They tilt trend lines.
segments.caption: They tilt trend lines.

segments.text: And they squash your charts.
segments.caption: And they squash your charts.

segments.text: So should you just delete them? Not so fast!
segments.caption: So should you just delete them? Not so fast!
